text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the vomiting and chest pain started, and what the pain feels like? Also, have you noticed any blood in your vomit or had any recent episodes of severe heartburn?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are in distress; your symptoms of forceful vomiting followed by sudden chest pain and coughing are concerning for a possible esophageal rupture. I will immediately request a CT scan of the chest to evaluate for this emergency. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray Findings: Free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation. Note: The requested CT_Chest test is not in the current data; only the Chest_X-ray results are available. Vital Signs: Temperature 37°C, Blood Pressure 90/68 mmHg, Heart Rate 107 bpm, Respiratory Rate 15 breaths/min. Chest Examination: Inspection shows fullness at the base of the neck; Auscultation reveals a crunching, rasping sound over the chest; Palpation suggests possible crepitus on the chest and neck.

speaker: Doctor
text: The findings of free mediastinal air, subcutaneous emphysema, and your vital instability strongly confirm a diagnosis of Boerhaave syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture)
